card.title: Minimum deviation — the symmetric ray through a prism

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A prism bends light twice (entry + exit); total deviation δ = i + e − A. As incidence rises from grazing, deviation falls to a MINIMUM then climbs — at that minimum the ray travels symmetrically (i = e, r₁ = r₂ = A/2), and the symmetry unlocks μ. Small-angle prisms (A ≲ 10°) deviate proportionally to (μ−1)A with no minimum hunt needed.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: δ = i + e − A (A = r₁ + r₂)  ·  minimum: μ = sin[(A + δm)/2] / sin(A/2), with i = e, r = A/2  ·  small-angle: δ ≈ (μ − 1)·A

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: The μ formula holds ONLY at minimum deviation (symmetric passage) for a single wavelength in a homogeneous prism. Small-angle form needs A in radians-ish smallness (≲10°) and paraxial rays. Both assume the prism surrounded by air (μ≈1).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Equilateral prism (A = 60°) with δm = 60° gives μ = sin60°/sin30° = √3 ≈ 1.732 — a favourite plug-in. Deviation is NOT always minimum: the NEB 2023 MCQ probes exactly this (symmetric passage is the condition, not a property). Immersed prisms rescale μ to relative index.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Prism A = 60°, μ = 1.5: at minimum deviation sin[(60+δm)/2]/sin30° = 1.5 → sin[(60+δm)/2] = 0.75 → (60+δm)/2 ≈ 48.6° → δm ≈ 37.2° (NEB 2022, 4-mark pattern with i = 40° incidence working). Check: symmetric ray, i = e = (A+δm)/2 ≈ 48.6°.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The formula measures ONE wavelength's μ — white light smears δm into a spectrum (dispersion, next unit). Surface imperfections and non-parallelism break symmetry; thick prisms add lateral displacement the thin-prism model ignores.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: At the δ minimum, dδ/di = 0 forces the reversible symmetric path i = e (Fermat/reversibility argument); then A = r₁+r₂ gives r = A/2, and Snell at entry sin i = μ·sin(A/2) with i = (A+δm)/2 from the δ relation — divide and the μ formula appears.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: See 'minimum deviation' → write i = e and r = A/2 immediately. 60°-prism + δm = 60° → μ = √3 on sight. Small-angle questions skip the minimum entirely: δ = (μ−1)A.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (1): deviation is minimum only for symmetric passage (MCQ). NEB 2022 (4): A = 60°, μ = 1.5 prism numerical with incidence/internal-angle working. Derive i–e–A–δ relation (asked via dispersion unit, 2023).
